review_notes: I read the whole 55-line file and the API lemmas it uses in CoefficientIdeal.lean and Primary.lean. I grepped for simp attributes there. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about simp behaviour or loops. The file uses `simp only` with hand-supplied lemmas. The main weakness is that the `C`-extension simp set is incomplete: the `≤` reflection lemma is `@[simp]`, but the equality and primary analogues are not. I did not recommend making `map_C_iInf` simp, because pushing `map` inward conflicts with the `←` direction used here, and I could not tell which direction is better for downstream uses.

findings.problem: The simp interface for extension along `C` is incomplete. `map_C_le_map_C_iff` is `@[simp]`, but the corresponding equality reflection exists only as the non-simp `Function.Injective`, so each use has to write `(map_C_injective (σ := σ)).eq_iff` by hand. `isPrimary_map_C_iff` is also a clean, unconditional iff (`(I.map C).IsPrimary ↔ I.IsPrimary`). It is not tagged `@[simp]`, so it has to be listed in every call. The proof therefore depends on a hand-assembled lemma list instead of the library's simp set.
findings.proposed_change: In CoefficientIdeal.lean add a named iff lemma, for example `map_C_inj : I.map C = J.map C ↔ I = J`, proved with `map_C_injective.eq_iff` and tagged `@[simp]`, matching `map_C_le_map_C_iff`. Consider tagging `isPrimary_map_C_iff` `@[simp]`, since its right-hand side is strictly simpler. The proof could then drop the `eq_iff` term and read `simp only [← map_C_iInf, map_C_inj, isPrimary_map_C_iff]`.
findings.benefit: Equalities and primary-ness of extended coefficient ideals normalise to the coefficient ideals. The `≤`, `=` and `IsPrimary` reflection rules would then form one consistent simp set. Callers would no longer need to restate `(map_C_injective (σ := σ)).eq_iff`.

findings.problem: `map_C_le_map_C_iff` is already `@[simp]`, but `map_C_iInf` is not. The proof therefore needs a reversed rewrite, `← map_C_iInf`, to fold the family before the simp lemma can fire. This is the orientation opposite to the stated lemma, and the file does not say why. The interface does not offer a canonical normal form for `Ideal.map C (⨅ i, I i)`. Plain `simp` on these goals cannot discharge them. Tests and users have to choose the direction with `simp only [map_C_iInf, ...]` or `rw` each time.
findings.proposed_change: Decide on one normal form and document it. Either state a dedicated `@[simp]` lemma in the folding direction, for instance `⨅ i, (I i).map C = (⨅ i, I i).map C` for the unbundled `C` form. Or keep `map_C_iInf` non-simp and add a comment in CoefficientIdeal.lean saying that it is deliberately left out of the simp set and should be used reversed. Do not add the forward direction as `@[simp]` while this file relies on `←`, because the two orientations would compete.
findings.benefit: Users get a predictable orientation for iInf-of-extensions. The two lemmas in this file could be closed by a lighter `simp` call, and the existing test `simp only [map_C_iInf, Ideal.mem_iInf]` would no longer conflict with the folding direction used here.
